the next Private pass; row NEW O-EDGE-CONFIG-NOT-DECLARED). Before this file only the zone's rate-limit rule was
declared and drift-read (tooling/edge-ratelimit-rule.json). That every served host was proxied was a one-off
fact (PB-05); the two WAF custom rules, the Access apps, the proxied flag of every DNS record and the tunnel

READ BY tooling/ops/check-edge-zone.mjs, in ops-watch.yml's weekly `edge-shield` job (and on any dispatch):
0 the live zone is what this file declares · 1 drift (a proxiable record DNS-only outside `dns.dnsOnly`, a
declared record or Access app missing, a live Access app nobody declared, a policy-id set or a WAF rule that
moved, or a gated host whose GET / no longer answers 302 to *.cloudflareaccess.com) · 2 COULD NOT LOOK.
Offline, tooling/ci/test/edge-zone.test.mjs holds this file's shape and its cross-file joins.
PROVIDER-NEUTRAL WHERE A NEUTRAL FORM EXISTS (the plan-portability addendum). The provider is ONE field,
`provider`; the zone id is never written here, it is resolved by name at read time. Every DNS record is
`{ name, type, content, ttl, proxied }` and `proxied` is the one Cloudflare-specific flag in it. The WAF rules,
the rate-limit rule, the Access apps and the tunnel ingress have no neutral form and live under `cloudflare`.
So a DNS-provider move is `node tooling/ops/check-edge-zone.mjs --export <file>` (local only): the records in this
shape plus the list of what has no equivalent, written to <file> and never to a log. tooling/ports/_non-port.json names the zone as declared, not ported.
🔴 `null` MEANS NOT YET MEASURED, NEVER 'ANY VALUE'. A field written null is noted on every run (a record's
content as an 8-char sha256 only: the ops-watch log is public) and is not compared; a field with a value is compared and its drift is exit 1. Nothing in this file
was read from the live zone in the lane that wrote it (it had no Cloudflare credential), so every value below
is one the repository already asserts elsewhere, cited per row, and every other value is null. The first local
`--export <file>` with CLOUDFLARE_READ_TOKEN fills them in a reviewed change; it never writes this file itself.
⚠️ RECORDS NOT DECLARED ARE PRINTED, NOT FAILED, unless they break the one rule PB-05 is about: a proxiable
record (A, AAAA, CNAME) that is DNS-only and is not in `dns.dnsOnly` is exit 1, declared or not. That is the
'100% of served hosts are proxied' fact made standing rather than one-off. Worker custom domains and routes
(services/*/wrangler.jsonc) are owned by those files and their deploys, and are not repeated here.
